info.name: SealDoc
info.summary: Turn stored documents into evidence: PDF/A-3B, trusted timestamp and chain of custody
info.description:
Nextcloud stores your documents. It does not, on its own, prove that a document has not changed since you filed it, or that it existed on the date you claim. For invoices, contracts and personnel records that have to survive a statutory retention period, that difference only becomes visible at the moment somebody asks, which is usually years later.
This app connects Nextcloud to SealDoc. Every document it processes comes back as a **PDF/A-3B** file validated against ISO 19005-3, carrying an **RFC 3161 timestamp** from a trusted authority, a **SHA-384 hash chain** and a **chain-of-custody** record, exported as a single evidence pack.
**How you use it**
- As a Flow (workflow) action: *when a file is created in /Invoices, seal it*. - The sealed file is written back next to the original, so it stays in the folder and the sharing you already have.
**What it does not do**
- It does not provide electronic signatures. It proves a document has not changed, not who agreed to it. Those are different questions. - The timestamps are RFC 3161 timestamps from a trusted authority. They are **not** qualified timestamps under eIDAS. - It is not an archive. It produces evidence designed to outlive the service; the file stays in your Nextcloud.
**Where the processing happens**
You choose. Point the app at the hosted service in the EU, or at your own self-hosted SealDoc instance. The app talks to nothing else.
info.author: Bryan van Rijn
